title: AppMission
description: An app-studio mission ledger record — a gated state machine over the 15-stage spine (intake → discovery → concept → concept-gate → architecture → architecture-gate → planning → plan-gate → scaffold → executing ↔ wave-review → acceptance-gate → registration → closed, plus the terminal aborted). Extracted after the tutor genesis pilot proved the shape end to end (D066 build-then-extract), not predicted ahead of a build. This describes the *projected* record as an API reader sees it (app-studio's `projection.project()`): the stored fields plus read-time derivations. The derived fields (`stageKind`, `isTerminal`, `gateContext`, `rewindTargets`, `pipeline`) are optional here on purpose — a producer emitting a stored row rather than a projection omits them, and they are recomputed, never persisted. Three append-only record lists ride along and only the first is a decision: `gateRecords` (owner verdicts), `sendBacks` (a note with no verdict), `rewinds` (owner-only backward jumps, D067).

id.description: Mission identifier. Stable for the mission's whole life.

class.description: What kind of work this is. `genesis` births a new app from an idea and therefore passes through `scaffold`; `feature` is a delta on an app that already exists and skips `scaffold` — same conception and planning machinery, no repo to birth.

appName.description: Functional name (D002) of the app this mission is about.

stage.description: Where the mission currently sits on the spine.

stageKind.description: DERIVED. What kind of stage `stage` is — the distinction is the point: `mechanical` advances itself, `dispatched` advances when an observable agent run consolidates, `gate` moves ONLY on a recorded owner decision, `terminal` never moves.

intake.description: The originating brief, as the owner wrote it. Free-form; never rewritten by the studio.

targetRepo.description: The app's repo, once it exists. Null until then — a genesis mission has no target before `scaffold`.

designMissionId.description: The linked design-studio mission, once the design subcontract is staged. Null when no design leg exists.

currentWave.description: Which wave `executing`/`wave-review` currently concerns. 0 until the first wave is authorized.

abortedFrom.description: Set only on abort — what the mission was doing when it stopped. `aborted` sits beside the spine rather than on it (reachable from anywhere), so the origin stage is recorded rather than inferred.

abortReason.description: Why it stopped. Empty string on a live mission.

gateRecords.description: Append-only owner decisions — never edited, never removed. A gate that repeats (wave-review) contributes one record per round.

gate.description: Which of the five gates this decision was made at.

outcome.description: The platform's gate vocabulary (D091), inherited whole. `approved` advances; `rejected` does not advance and is binding direction for the next round. There is deliberately no third `send-back` member — see `sendBacks`.

notes.description: The owner's own words. On a rejection this is binding direction folded into the next dispatched round.

waveReviewNext.description: Only meaningful on an APPROVED `wave-review`, the one gate with more than one forward target: `next-wave` proceeds into the already-planned next wave, `replan` returns to planning first (the rolling-wave default), `accept` declares the build finished and moves to the acceptance gate. Carried rather than inferred — inferring it would be the studio deciding something only the owner may decide. Null everywhere else.

wave.description: Which wave this decision was about, when the gate repeats. Null on the once-only gates.

sendBacks.description: Notes with NO verdict, deliberately their own list rather than a third `outcome` member. A send-back records that a gate cannot be honestly evaluated as instrumented; it is never folded into a dispatched agent's direction. Collapsing it into `gateRecords` would lose exactly that distinction.

rewinds.description: Owner-only backward jumps to an earlier gate stage (D067). The direction rides along as a synthetic rejection at the target gate, so a rewind needs no second fold-in mechanism.

toStage.description: A rewind may only land on a gate stage strictly behind the mission.

direction.description: What the owner wants done differently on the way back through.

gateContext.description: DERIVED. What the owner needs in order to decide the gate the mission is sitting at. Null when the mission is not at a gate — the absence is the signal, so a console never has to ask a second question to find out.

subject.description: What this gate's decision is actually about. A gate attests what its own subject can evidence (D091).

bindingDirection.description: The directions carried from every prior rejection at this gate, oldest first — `null` when the gate has never rejected. A list, not a single string: a gate that rejects twice binds the owner to both directions, and the earlier one does not stop being binding because a second arrived. Length tracks `priorRounds`.

priorRounds.description: How many times this gate has already rejected.

approvalRequires.description: Present only at `wave-review`: an approval there is incomplete without one of these.

rewindTargets.description: DERIVED. The gates strictly behind the mission — where a rewind could legally land. Empty on a terminal mission.

pipeline.description: DERIVED, and deliberately unconstrained. The current stage's dispatch state (running / dead / blocked), which lives in an artifact rather than the ledger. Shape belongs to app-studio's dispatch layer and is not a cross-hexagon port; a consumer that needs it reads app-studio's own API.

missionStage.description: The mission spine (spec-app-studio.md §2, D093). `aborted` is terminal and sits beside the spine rather than on it.

waveReviewNext.description: Where an approved `wave-review` sends the mission — the owner's choice, and the reason `wave-review` is the one gate whose approval carries a payload. Nullable at its use site via oneOf-with-null: that form keeps one shared definition of the vocabulary and generates a clean nullable enum in Python and TypeScript. jsonschema2pojo 1.2.1 does not follow a oneOf, so the two nullable enum fields (`abortedFrom`, `gateRecords[].waveReviewNext`) surface as java.lang.Object in the Java binding — a known, tested property (AppStudioContractsTest), preferred over the alternative: writing the vocabulary out inline at each nullable site fixes Java but makes datamodel-code-generator emit a plain Enum rather than this repo's StrEnum, where a Python consumer's `record.waveReviewNext == "replan"` would silently be False. A visible cast beats a silent mismatch.

missionGateStage.description: The five stages that move ONLY on a recorded owner decision.
